subject: Copywriting
title: Michelin: Stars as Copy
description: One-minute skill: Michelin: Stars as Copy.

hook.text: A tire company decides which restaurants are the world's best.

buildup.text: In 1900, Michelin created a restaurant guide to encourage driving—and tire sales.

discovery.text: Michelin's genius: they never describe the food. One star, two stars, three stars.

twist.text: Chefs have returned stars, saying the pressure destroys creativity. The copy system meant to celebrate became a cage.

climax.text: Michelin stars prove that the most powerful luxury copy isn't words—it's a symbol everyone agrees means excellence.

punchline.text: No words, just stars. A tire company writes the language of fine dining.

quiz.question: Why did Michelin originally create its restaurant guide?
options: To sell tires by encouraging driving
